subtype: Leaning closer to share and secrets [Expressing]
passage:
“Psst, Urmila,” whispered Sumit, leaning across the desk. “Guess what happened to Sir's chair yesterday.” Urmila leaned in, eyes wide. Behind them, Ravi stopped writing and stared at his book. His shoulders had sunk a little.
Urmila noticed. She sat back. “Ravi, come listen. Sumit's got a funny story.”
“It's not that funny,” said Sumit, but he shifted over. “Okay, listen.” He told it out loud, and all three of them laughed.
Ravi grinned. “That's really funny.”

qa.q: Who leaned across the desk to whisper to Urmila?
qa.a: Sumit leaned across the desk to whisper.

qa.q: What did Sumit's leaning in and whispering show, and how might Ravi have felt?
qa.a: It showed trust and a wish to share, but Ravi's sinking shoulders and stare at his book suggest he felt left out. He might also just have been focusing on his work.

qa.q: What did Urmila do that helped?
qa.a: She noticed Ravi and invited him to listen, so the story became a shared one and nobody was left out.

qa.q: What would change if Sumit had kept whispering?
qa.a: Ravi might have felt excluded and stayed quiet, and Urmila might have felt caught between them.

grounding: Leaning in to whisper signals trust and inclusion, and those left out may feel excluded; including them helps.

subtype: Leaning closer to share and secrets [Expressing]
passage: I'm Joseph. At lunch I leaned toward Reena to show her a funny picture on my dad's phone. We both laughed so hard we had to hold our stomachs. Across the table Kabir's face went still, and he started stirring his dal. I realised he couldn't see and he hadn't been asked. I felt a bit bad. So I turned the screen so he could see it too. “Sorry, Kabir, look!” He laughed as well, and the stirring stopped. I want to remember that leaning in together feels great for the two people, but the others notice.

qa.q: What did Joseph show Reena on his dad's phone?
qa.a: Joseph showed Reena a funny picture.

qa.q: What was Kabir probably feeling when his face went still and he stirred his dal, and what else could it be?
qa.a: Probably left out, since he could not see the picture and had not been asked. It might also just have been that he was focused on his lunch.

qa.q: What did Joseph do that repaired the moment?
qa.a: Joseph noticed Kabir, turned the screen so he could see it and said sorry, so all three could share the joke.

qa.q: How might Reena feel about Joseph turning the screen?
qa.a: Probably happy to share, since she was already laughing with Joseph. She may not have noticed Kabir until Joseph did.

grounding: Leaning close to share signals trust; those left out may feel excluded and including them is kind.

subtype: Leaning closer to share and secrets [Expressing]
passage: Group-work note, Wednesday. Indu, Class 6. In the science group today, Damini and Shruti sat with their heads almost touching, whispering and giggling over a drawing in Damini's notebook. The third member, Ravi, sat holding his pencil, looking from one to the other, then out of the window. He tried twice to join in and wasn't heard. I walked past and said quietly to Damini, “Looks like a good secret. Is there room for three?” Damini glanced at Ravi, then turned her notebook round. “It's Shruti's cat as a scientist.” Ravi laughed and added goggles. By the end, all three of them were leaning in.

qa.q: What was the drawing in Damini's notebook?
qa.a: It was Shruti's cat as a scientist.

qa.q: What was Ravi feeling while he looked out of the window?
qa.a: Ravi probably felt left out and a bit lonely, since his two tries to join in weren't heard.

qa.q: How did Indu help without scolding?
qa.a: Indu quietly asked if there was room for three, which reminded Damini to include Ravi without embarrassing anyone.

qa.q: What did the leaning in show about Damini and Shruti?
qa.a: It showed their trust and closeness, though it also shut Ravi out until Damini turned the notebook round.

grounding: Shows children leaning in to whisper as a sign of trust, how it can leave others out, and making room for them.

subtype: Leaning closer to share and secrets [Expressing]
passage: Sunday. Deepak's diary. At Chachi's house, Devika leaned right in next to me on the sofa and tilted her phone so only I could see. It was a video of her dog falling off the bed. We were shaking with laughter, trying to be quiet. Then I saw my little cousin Mitali standing by the door, watching us, holding her doll really tight. She looked like she wanted to come but didn't know if she was allowed. I remembered feeling like that at Diwali when the big cousins had a secret. So I said, “Mitali, come see! It's a dog.” Devika moved the phone into the middle. Mitali squeezed in and laughed the loudest.

qa.q: What was the video on Devika's phone?
qa.a: It was a video of her dog falling off the bed.

qa.q: What was Mitali feeling as she stood by the door holding her doll tight?
qa.a: Mitali probably felt left out and unsure whether she was allowed to join.

qa.q: What did Deepak do that helped, and why?
qa.a: Deepak invited Mitali over and Devika moved the phone to the middle, so the shared fun included her too 😊

qa.q: What did leaning in together mean to Devika?
qa.a: For Devika, leaning in was a way of sharing something funny with a friend she trusts.

grounding: Shows children leaning close to share a phone screen as trust, and including a left-out child.

subtype: Leaning closer to share and secrets [Expressing]
passage: On the walk home along the canal, Nandini leaned close to Jagdish, cupped her hand round his ear and whispered, “I've saved up for Masterji's retirement gift. A new umbrella. Don't tell.” Jagdish grinned and whispered back, “I'll add my share.” Behind them, Kamla, who had only joined the village school that month, slowed down and looked at the ground. Nandini saw her. She dropped back and walked beside her. “We're planning a secret surprise for Masterji,” she said, low. “Want to be in it?” Kamla's head came up. “Can I make a card? I can draw umbrellas.” The three of them leaned in together.

qa.q: What gift had Nandini saved up for?
qa.a: Nandini saved up for a new umbrella as Masterji's retirement gift.

qa.q: What was Kamla feeling when she slowed down and looked at the ground?
qa.a: Kamla probably felt left out and lonely, being new and watching the others share a secret.

qa.q: How did Nandini make the secret kind rather than excluding?
qa.a: Nandini noticed Kamla, dropped back and invited her into the surprise, so the whispering brought her in.

qa.q: What did Nandini's whisper show about her friendship with Jagdish?
qa.a: It showed trust, since she shared a secret plan with him and he joined in at once.

grounding: Shows a child leaning in to whisper a secret as trust and inclusion, and kindly bringing in a child who was left out.

subtype: Leaning closer to share and secrets [Expressing]
passage:
At break in a Berlin schoolyard, Ines leaned in close to Selin, cupping her hand round Selin's ear. "My cat had kittens last night. Five!"

Selin squealed, and Ines pulled out her phone. Their heads almost touched as they bent over the tiny screen.

Behind them, Johanna, who had only joined the class that week, hovered with her lunchbox, looking at the ground. Selin noticed first and nudged Ines. Ines hesitated. The kittens were a bit of a secret. Then she tilted the phone. "Johanna, want to see? They're so small their eyes aren't open."

Johanna stepped in, and three heads bent over the screen.

qa.q: How many kittens did Ines's cat have?
qa.a: Five.

qa.q: Why did Ines hesitate before tilting the phone?
qa.a: She felt a little protective of her news, since the kittens were a bit of a secret shared with Selin; she was torn between keeping it close and including Johanna.

qa.q: What small choice made Johanna feel included?
qa.a: Ines tilted the phone and invited Johanna by name to see the kittens.

qa.q: How might Johanna feel watching the two heads almost touching?
qa.a: As a newcomer she likely felt left out and lonely, which is why she hovered and looked at the ground.

grounding: It shows children leaning in close to whisper and share a phone screen as a sign of trust, and including a left-out newcomer.
